sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.text: Makro missed sales plan by R1.9m (0.31%) but finished R26.8m (4.43%) ahead of last year, while margin fell R15.8m (33.26%) short of plan — a rate problem far larger than the sales shortfall. The miss was concentrated in three regions: Western Cape (R5.5m), Eastern Cape (R3.8m) and Mpumalanga (R3.2m), while Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo and Free State all traded ahead of plan. OTD stood at 90.7% for the period, with Omni Operations explicitly prioritising OTD recovery.

sections.title: Divisional Sales Variance vs Plan (Weekly) — individually sourced, does not fully reconcile to total (see note)

executive_facts.statement: Western Cape, Eastern Cape and Mpumalanga together drove the national plan miss, while Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo and Free State all traded ahead of plan.
Margin underperformance (R15.8m vs Plan) was roughly eight times the size of the sales miss (R1.9m vs Plan), pointing to a margin-rate problem rather than a volume problem this week.
Mbombela was Mpumalanga's only underperforming store and accounted for the region's entire R3.2m plan miss.

The 5-day trading period (1–5 July) showed sales R47.5m (10.80%) ahead of last year across all three divisions, but margin fell R2.9m (10.68%) behind LY over the same period — the same margin-vs-sales divergence pattern as the weekly result.
OTD stood at 90.7% for the period, with Omni Operations explicitly prioritising OTD recovery alongside HWD execution and waybill cancellation process communication.

sections.text: Margin eroded roughly eight times faster than sales missed plan (R15.8m vs R1.9m), and virtually all of the national shortfall was concentrated in three regions — Western Cape, Eastern Cape and Mpumalanga — pointing to a pricing/promotional-execution issue rather than a broad demand problem.

sections.title: Customer Feedback Themes
sections.text:
• Shopping experience — layout, navigation, parking, trolley condition, aisle congestion.
  • Staff availability — customers want more visible, faster, more knowledgeable staff at peak times.
  • Pricing — requests for lower prices, more promotions, clearer promotional communication, reward points.
  • Stock availability — broader ranges, fuller shelves, better replenishment to reduce out-of-stocks.
  • Checkout & queues — more tills open, faster checkout, more self-checkout at peak times.

provenance.extraction_notes: Scoped to executive-level headline, regional, and priority metrics from the Finance Update, Key Priorities, Customer, Associate, and Omni Operations sections. Store- and article-level long-tail detail (per-region bottom-5-article breakdowns, individual SKU variances) was intentionally excluded as sub-executive detail, per the source's own regional appendices — available on request if needed. The regional sales-variance-vs-plan breakdown reconciles to the stated total within R58k (rounding across 7 rounded regional figures). The divisional (Food/Liquor/General Merchandise) variance figures quoted in the source commentary do NOT reconcile to the stated total sales variance in either direction: they sum to -R1.2m vs a stated total of -R1.9m vs Plan (R0.7m gap), and to R46.9m vs a stated R47.5m vs LY for the 5-day period (R0.6m gap). This is a genuine gap in the source document, not a rounding artifact -- most likely trade outside the three core divisions (e.g. BP fuel, wholesale-only lines) that isn't broken out in this commentary. Per the reconciliation-first rule, these divisional figures are presented as individually-sourced KPIs rather than as a breakdown_table, since a breakdown_table would falsely assert they sum to the total. Recommend requesting the full divisional P&L extract if an exact reconciled divisional breakdown is needed.
